system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation: time-temperature superposition principle for viscoelastic materials and Arrhenius-type degradation kinetics. The 75-year service life requires that the elastomer's creep compliance (J(t)) remains below 1.1×J₀ (initial compliance) and ozone-induced crack growth rate must be <0.01 mm/year to maintain deflection drift below 10%.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
1. Add 3mm thick ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (EPDM) protective barrier layer with 30% carbon black loading (USER CONSTRAINT: ozone resistance requirement)
2. Incorporate 15% by weight of pre-stressed aramid fiber reinforcement in elastomer matrix (USER CONSTRAINT: stiffness drift limitation)
3. Install embedded strain gauges during manufacturing with wireless transmission capability (USER CONSTRAINT: no replacement access)
4. Use vulcanization process with 5-minute dwell time at 150°C (CALCULATED: optimal crosslink density for creep resistance)
5. Apply zinc diethyldithiocarbamate (ZDEC) antioxidant at 2 phr (ASSUMPTION: sufficient for 75-year protection)

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Standard practice uses unreinforced natural rubber bearings with no monitoring. This implementation increases material cost by ~40% due to EPDM and aramid reinforcement, but eliminates the need for replacement inspections (which are typically required every 15-20 years). The wireless monitoring adds ~5% to bearing cost but provides continuous data without access requirements.

EXECUTIVE TEST — 
Protocol: Subject 10 prototype bearings to accelerated aging (70°C for 6 months) followed by 10 million load cycles at 20% above design load. Monitor deflection drift and crack propagation weekly.
Instruments: Laser deflection measurement (±0.01mm accuracy), crack detection microscope (5µm resolution), embedded strain gauges (±5µε accuracy).
Pass/Fail: Deflection drift >10% of design or crack length >3mm at any point.
Duration: 6 months aging + 3 months cycling (equivalent to 75 years service).
